assessments.reasoning: The Python Software Foundation's official 3.13.0 publisher source was retrieved at the registered immutable commit URL. The complete captured body and lines 415–444 match their frozen SHA-256 digests. The pinned finally paragraph describes an unhandled exception being saved, normally reraised at the end, displaced as the context of a new exception, or discarded when the finally clause transfers control by executing return, break or continue. The frozen statement expressly requires an executed transfer out of the active finally clause, so a break or continue within a loop that leaves the cleanup running is outside its scope. The adjacent control-transfer discussion and return example ground the description. As an implementation challenge, exact CPython 3.13.0 compiler lines 1551–1561, 1610–1633 and 3281–3307 show exception-state cleanup when crossing FINALLY_END and stopping unwind at the intended loop. The claim concerns the documented 3.13.0 rule without extrapolating warnings or later edition changes.

limitations: The asserted rule applies to a saved exception and an executed control transfer out of the active finally clause. A break or continue confined to a loop inside that clause is outside the assertion.
